title: Onboarding Ops Manifest and Access Playbook
author: Asha Patel
summary: A single-source playbook that standardizes operational handoffs for new hires, prescribes access governance to reduce permission sprawl ("access entropy"), and defines measurable SLAs for role activation across engineering and product teams.
audience: Hiring managers, people-ops partners, IT/cloud-admins, security, team leads
body:
Purpose

This playbook documents the operational steps, approvals, and guardrails required to activate a new team member at Redwood with minimal friction and minimal long-term permission proliferation ("access entropy"). It is intended to be used during hiring offers, the preboarding window, and the first 30 days after start.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time and contractor hires who require accounts or access to Redwood systems (cloud consoles, code repos, internal dashboards, ticketing, production-facing tools).
- Excludes strictly guest observers with no credentials (see visitor-access-runbook).

Definitions

- Access entropy: the tendency for an individual to accumulate more privileged accounts and roles than necessary over time, increasing risk and audit surface.
- Role Activation: the moment a user can perform job-critical tasks (first commit, deploy to staging, view customer data) after onboarding.
- Just-in-Time (JIT) access: ephemeral privilege granted for a bounded window via automation.

Ownership and Contacts

- People Ops (Primary owner): coordinates hiring handoff and verification for non-technical access.
- IT/Cloud Admins: manage cloud and infra accounts, single sign-on (SSO) groups.
- Security: approves elevated privilege requests and reviews exceptions.
- Manager: validates role responsibilities and confirms required tool set.

Onboarding Ops Manifest (runbook)

1) Hiring acceptance -> Handoff (T-5 business days recommended)
   - People Ops sends the Hiring Handoff packet to the hiring manager and IT owner. Packet includes start date, role profile, repo/team names, office/location, and required seat/license list.
   - Manager completes the Role Activation Form (template link) indicating minimum privileges required for day 1 and for week 1.

2) Preboarding (T-3 to T-1 business days)
   - Create SSO account stub and invite to Slack.
   - Provision base accounts: Google Workspace, Okta, corporate laptop ticket, identity group membership to "all-employees" and "engineering" or equivalent.
   - Open laptop procurement/ship ticket and include baseline security imaging profile.
   - IT configures MFA requirement and sends enrollment steps.

3) Day 0 / Day 1
   - First-touch checklist for manager and buddy: welcome message, calendar sync, orientation block, and walk-through of the Role Activation Plan.
   - Grant scoped access required for day 1 tasks only. Examples: dev repo read + onboarding branch create, staging dashboard view, internal wiki edit.
   - Ensure JIT tool (temporary escalation) is installed and manager has request path (if extra access needed).

4) Week 1 (Day 2–7)
   - Validate access for the top 3 role-critical systems defined on the Role Activation Form.
   - Schedule a 1:1 with IT owner to request additional group membership if needed with justification.
   - Begin security orientation: least-privilege guidelines, secret management, and incident reporting flow.

5) Week 2–4: Role hardening and entropy prevention
   - People Ops runs entitlement review: confirm only required groups were granted.
   - If elevated privileges were used via JIT, ensure that they were documented and set to expire automatically.
   - Manager performs a 30-day gate: either confirm continued privileges or file a reduction request.

Access Entropy Mitigation Controls (practical guardrails)

- Principle of Minimum Necessary: every requested role must include an explicit business justification and an expected expiration.
- Default to timeboxed access: non-essential privileges auto-expire after 14 days unless extended via an approval flow.
- Require manager-attestation at 30, 90, and 180 days for any elevated roles.
- Use ephemeral credentials for production deployments and require audit annotations on each elevated session.
- Quarterly entitlement sweep: People Ops + Security run automated reports to detect unusual group membership growth.

Role Activation Checklist (manager-facing, actionable)

- Before Day 1: submit Role Activation Form (link) with minimum list of services and an initial JIT plan.
- Day 0: confirm Slack invite and calendar items created.
- Day 1: ensure access to code repo (read), onboarding docs, internal wiki, and dev cluster (staging view).
- Week 1: confirm ability to run local test suite and create a PR to the onboarding repo.
- Week 2: validate data access boundaries and sign the data-handling checklist if applicable.
- Day 30: complete 30-day access attestation in the HR portal.

Access Matrix (example)

| System | Typical initial access | Day-30 expected | Owner to approve | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| GitHub - team repos | read, write to onboarding branch | read, write (pr) | Team lead | No prod+merge rights until code review policy satisfied |
| Staging Dashboard | view | view | DevOps owner | Production view requires JIT request |
| Prod Deploy Console | none | none (JIT only) | Security | JIT with recorded session and approval |
| Analytics / Customer PII | none | role-based read after training | Data owner | Training required before access |

Note: The table above is illustrative; managers must complete the Role Activation Form for role-specific variants.

Approval and Exception Flow (short)

1) Manager submits access request in the provisioning portal with business justification.
2) IT auto-provisions baseline access; any privileged role triggers Security review.
3) Security approves or requests modifications within 48 hours. If urgent, use the emergency access workflow and notify People Ops.

Escalation steps if activation misses SLOs:

- T+1 business day missed: People Ops pings manager and IT owner for status update.
- T+3 business days missed: Director-level intervention (manager's manager notified).
- T+5 business days missed: CSAT impact review and potential remediation (temporary contractor or pairing).

Operational SLAs and Metrics

- Target time-to-basic-activation (email + Slack + workspace): 2 business days (95th percentile).
- Target time-to-role-activation (top 3 systems functional): 5 business days (90th percentile).
- JIT escalation review window: Security responses within 48 hours.

KPIs to track monthly:

- % of hires meeting day-1 basic activation SLA
- Median days to role activation
- Number of privileged roles granted per active employee (entropy metric)
- # of JIT sessions and % with audit annotations

Automation recipes and CLI snippets

- Example: SSO invite (Okta) via CLI
  okta-client invite --email new-hire@example.com --groups "all-employees,engineering" --send-invite true

- Example: Create timeboxed IAM role (pseudo-YAML)
  iam-create-role --name "temp-prod-deploy-${USER}" --policy deployer --expiry 2027-03-15T23:59:00Z --annotate "JIT: code-review-needed"

Manager Responsibilities (quick list)

- Fill Role Activation Form before offer acceptance (preferred).
- Assign a first-week buddy and schedule time to validate access.
- Certify 30/90/180-day attestation for escalated permissions.
- If access is no longer required, file a reduction request within 5 business days.

Security and Compliance Notes

- All access for customer-sensitive systems requires training completion and a signed data-handling checklist prior to approval.
- Audit logs for JIT sessions must be retained for at least 1 year and are subject to quarterly review.

Appendix A — Role Activation Form (field list)

- Candidate name
- Start date
- Role title and brief responsibilities
- Systems required on Day 1 (top 3)
- Systems required by Day 30 (top 3)
- Justification for any elevated privileges
- Manager attestation checkbox

Appendix B — Common failure modes and remediation

- Missing laptop: escalate to IT within 24 hours and schedule a temporary cloud desktop image.
- Missing MFA enrollment: block production access until enrollment complete; provide step-by-step enrollment doc.
- Excessive permission grants: People Ops triggers entitlement review and offers remediation pathways (revoke, re-scope, or justify).

Revision history and governance

- This document is reviewed quarterly by People Ops and Security. Significant process changes must be submitted as a PR to the People Ops handbook and approved by the Head of People Ops.

Contact and feedback

- For operational issues: people-ops@redwood.ai
- For security exceptions: security-requests@redwood.ai
- For questions about this playbook: asha.patel@redwood.ai
notes: This playbook is intentionally prescriptive: it balances fast time-to-activation with strict entropy controls. Use templates linked in the Role Activation Form to reduce variability across teams.
